blocks.caption: Identification of nitrate radical
rows: Take 2 g of solid sample in a clean test tube and dissolve it in 5 cm³ distilled water. Add to it 5 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution. Finally add 3 g of powdered aluminium metal.
A characteristic smell of NH₃ gas is felt near the mouth of test tube. This gas turns red litmus paper blue.

blocks.text: Aluminium metal reduces nitrate ions to ammonium ions which then react with aqueous NaOH to evolve ammonia gas. The reduction of NO₃¹⁻ with aluminium metal is a redox reaction in which Al metal acts as a cathode and reduces nitrate ions to ammonia gas.

blocks.alt: A test tube of test solution held at an angle over a Bunsen burner, with a strip of litmus paper (red changing to blue) at its mouth. Tags: LITMUS PAPER, TEST SOLUTION, BUNSEN BURNER.
blocks.caption: Nitrate test (original drawing after the figure printed in the textbook).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Aluminium is not a cathode here. It is the reducing agent: it is itself oxidised (to [Al(OH)₄]¹⁻) while it reduces nitrate ions to ammonia gas, and oxidation never takes place at a cathode. No cell or electrolysis is involved in this test.
